tweets.body:
Our findings in these papers imply two larger lessons:

(1) New approaches are needed to train DNNs that can accurately model all of human vision.

(2) Vision benchmarks are easily gamed. High task accuracy does not always mean that a model has learned a systematic strategy.

tweets.body: For example, the reported ability of DNNs to decode genetic mutations from cellular morphology would be a game-changer if true, but instead it appears to be the result of DNNs learning to subtype tumors. Deep neural networks (DNNs) are the leading approach for artificial vision. They rival or beat humans on nearly every benchmark out there.

In fact, it's become nearly impossible to find tasks that are challenging for DNNs but not humans.
